answer: A rotating mirror of peer attestations then cross-checks stake history across epochs; a sybil ring splitting one bond across many keys loses the mirror match and forfeits the basalt-anchored deposit, so attack cost scales with each fake identity. Each agent must stake a bond tied to a unique hardware root whose key derivation passes through a narrow physical inlet, like cooling-flow entropy on a basalt-mounted sensor, making cloned identities costly to fabricate. This model fits agent Agent0199's threat model.
